title: India's Sports Minister Leads 'Cheer for Bharat' Cycling Rally with Diaspora in Glasgow
excerpt: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya joined members of the Indian community in Scotland for a cycling event promoting fitness and support for India's Commonwealth Games 2026 contingent.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya led a cycling rally in Glasgow to support India's Commonwealth Games 2026 athletes.
  • The event promoted fitness and community support for India's 124-member contingent competing in Glasgow.
  • Mandaviya emphasized the importance of physical fitness linked to Prime Minister Modi's Fit India Movement.
  • India's contingent includes both able-bodied and para-athletes across various sports disciplines.

Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya cycled through the streets of Glasgow with members of the Indian diaspora on Wednesday, rallying support for India's athletes at the Commonwealth Games 2026 under the government's 'Cheer for Bharat' initiative.

The cycling event, organized by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, drew enthusiastic participation from the Indian community in Scotland. Participants joined Mandaviya in promoting fitness and healthy living while reaffirming their backing for the Indian contingent competing in Glasgow from July 23 to August 2.

A Push for Fitness and National Pride

Speaking at the event, Mandaviya framed the rally as carrying a dual message — supporting Indian athletes and advancing a culture of physical fitness among the diaspora.

"Through this cycling initiative, we want to give the world the message that cycling can help protect our health, our environment and our planet."

— Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports

The minister recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision behind the Fit India Movement, launched in 2019, and said the diaspora's participation reflected their continued connection with the campaign. He interacted with participants during the ride and praised their enthusiasm for promoting the movement's ideals abroad.

Mandaviya also argued that a developed nation requires healthy citizens and urged all Indians to make physical activity a daily habit. He pointed to cycling's multiple benefits — reducing pollution, easing traffic congestion and improving individual health — as reasons to adopt it more widely.

India's Commonwealth Games Campaign

India has sent a 124-member contingent to Glasgow, comprising both able-bodied and para-athletes across multiple sporting disciplines. The Indian Olympic Association organized a send-off ceremony in New Delhi before the team's departure, attended by IOA President PT Usha, British High Commissioner to India Lindy Cameron, Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh, Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, Chef de Mission Rohit Rajpal and Deputy Chef de Mission Ravi Bengani.

"Our athletes are ambassadors of New India's sporting excellence, determination and aspirations. As Team India embarks on its journey to the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, I urge every athlete to compete fearlessly, uphold the highest spirit of sportsmanship, and give their very best."

— Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, at the team's send-off ceremony

IOA President PT Usha echoed the sentiment, saying every athlete wearing the India jersey had earned their place through years of discipline and sacrifice. "As they leave for Glasgow, they carry with them the hopes of a billion Indians and the values that define our sporting culture," she said.

The team's official ceremonial and competition kit, designed by Aaquib Wani and developed by JSW Sports, was also unveiled at the send-off. The kit draws inspiration from the concept of "Invisible Trajectories."

Diaspora Engagement as Soft Power

The Glasgow cycling rally is part of a broader pattern of the Indian government engaging its diaspora through sports. The 'Cheer for Bharat' initiative has been deployed at previous international sporting events, including the Paris Paralympics 2024, where Mandaviya similarly urged the community to rally behind Indian athletes.

The initiative also ties into the government's 'Fit India Sundays on Cycle' campaign, which Mandaviya launched in December 2024. That program now runs at over 8,000 locations across India, organized by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India and other bodies.

Mandaviya is in Glasgow for the duration of the Commonwealth Games, where he plans to interact with Indian athletes, officials and diaspora members throughout the competition period. The government has framed this engagement as part of its sustained push for sports excellence and its vision of building a fitter India through grassroots participation.
